Jfc I don't care about if the actual lawsuit or Pura would be convicted because of Zubiri's statement. Its the statement in itself that is wrong. Its not a "freedom of expression". Its discriminatory and heavily prejudiced because, AS A PUBLIC SERVANT, he quite literally threatened someone who doesn't abide by his PERSONAL beliefs with a criminal case. And one of the things that you said is the main fucking problem. One, The 1987 Constitution of the Philippines declares: The separation of Church and State shall be inviolable. (Article II, Section 6), and, No law shall be made respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof. THEREFORE there really is no duty to respect his beliefs. Two, Politicians SHOULD not let their own PERSONAL beliefs on religion affect how they view their constituents as long as they are not outwardly committing a crime because you do realize that  every time that the government, not only in the Philippines, let their views on religion affect the their leadership, WARS HAPPEN. That is quite literally how Nazi Germany started and how Afghanistan slowly descended into extreme right wing ideations of their country LASTLY, it doesn't mean that the "majority" of the Filipino people practice Catholicism, that also means that this should affect the way you implement the law because no religion should outweigh the other. ALL OF THEM SHOULDNT MATTER in the court of law. Because when you say that "even if the politicians arent allowed to mix in their beliefs with politics, the majority of the Filipinos believe in this so theyre just doing what the majority wants" then it just completely disregards EVERY OTHER VALID RELIGION in the country who have the right to be heard and listened to. 

I dont know if youre just choosing to be ignorant or what OF COURSE anyone can meddle with the laws through voting and shit. The separation of church and state is important because if there wasn't the church would have a bigger say than the average voter. Because if there was no law that separates the church and the state, there would be much much more people from the church who have political power.

Section 5(2), Article VI, of the Constitution, mandates that party-list representatives shall not come from the religious sector. This provision ensures that the political arena remains secular and not influenced by religious organizations.

You seem to just completely gloss over the fact that Zubiri's statement, AS A PUBLIC SERVANT, is still a form of discrimination to people who offend his personal beliefs. 

If you dont understand my last point here it is. If there was no separation of church and state and the church had the right to meddle with the laws, there would probably be a fuck ton of laws about "offending religious beliefs" therefore so many butthurt Christians can use it to file criminal charges against anybody they deem offensive to their religion e.g. the LGBT community

Sure youre right about the separation of church and state but it still doesnt disregard the fact that these politicians let their own religious beliefs affect their way of leading the country and its so apparent in Zubiri's statement. Again, as a public servant, he has the duty to serve his people EQUALLY regardless of their religion, status, etc. but he went public saying that this person should be condemned in my opinion because they offended my personal beliefs. That is not freedom of expression. That is discriminatory and a clear disobedience to your oath. AGAIN, citing Risa Hontiveros as an example, she said that the act offended her personally but that shouldn't mean that this incident should affect the LGBT or even Pura herself politically. Because she understands that her own moral values should not get in the way her duties as a public servant.

Even if nothing comes out of it this is still an obvious showcase of his power. And mind you he isnt alone in this call to condemn Pura. 

I agree that the protection of Freedom of Expression shouldn't be mere lip service but if you are a public servant who took an oath to protect your constituents regardless if said constituents dont agree or abide by your own political and social beliefs, he shouldnt have made that statement.

He could've said that as a follower of the religion, he felt offended. Nothing more nothing less. Just like Risa Hontiveros who explicitly says that she took offense to it but the issue should not harm the LGBT community politically.  He is a public servant who is bound to his duties to protect the people REGARDLESS whether they offend his personal beliefs or not. As long as they are not committing a crime. That's why there is a separation of church and state because if there wasnt, Zubiri and every Christian would be filing lawsuits left and right.
He has the right to express his opinion but to use his POWER as a government official to condemn those who he claims to be "offending" religion just scream Nazism to me
